title: The Dove, Let Loose in Eastern Skies
description: The Dove, Let Loose in Eastern Skies in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Moore wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 273, “Faith”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The dove, let loose in East-ern skies, Re-turn-ing fond-ly home, Ne'er stoops to earth her wing, nor flies Where id-le war-blers roam;

lines: The dove, let loose in Eastern skies,
Ne'er stoops to earth her wing, nor flies
But high she shoots through air and light,
Where nothing earthly bounds her flight,
So grant me, Lord, from every snare
To urge my course to Thee:
No sin to cloud, no lure to stay,
My soul, as home she springs;
Thy sunshine on her joyful way,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Thomas Moore died in 1852.
credits: Words by Thomas Moore (1779–1852), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
